name: assets
description: Store and retrieve content-addressed assets — immutable, hash-identified, shareable across venues. Load when you need versioned documents, shared definitions, or binary content.

content.inline:
## Assets and content references
An asset is immutable metadata identified by its hash. Its bytes are resolved separately through one content-reference seam.

- store `{metadata, contentText?}` -> `{ref, id}`; `ref` is the DID URL ending `/a/<hash>`.
- get `{ref}` -> metadata; content `{ref}` -> bytes plus `contentType`; list shows assets; pin `{ref}` snapshots metadata locally.
- Asset refs include a bare hash, `a/<hash>`, `o/...`, `w/...`, `v/...`, or a DID URL.
- Content refs additionally include `file://<root>/<path>`, `dlfs/<drive>/<path>`, and owner-scoped DID/DLFS paths. Raw file/DLFS refs have bytes but no asset metadata.

Content conventions (inside metadata and covered by the asset hash):
- `content: {inline: "text", contentType: "text/plain"}` — small body directly in metadata.
- `content: {sha256: ...}` — pins uploaded/external bytes (drift fails loudly).
- `content: {dlfs: "dlfs/drive/path"}` — binds to a DLFS file; live unless sha256-pinned.

Assets are immutable: to update, store a new version and re-point references. Use assets for anything shared, versioned, or cross-venue; use `w/` workspace or file/DLFS storage for mutable content.
